name: Bahla Fort
description: Rising from a green palm oasis at the foot of Oman's Jebel Akhdar mountains, Bahla Fort is a vast stronghold of mud-brick walls and towers set on stone foundations. It was built when the Banu Nebhan tribe dominated the region, between the 12th and late 15th centuries. In 1987 it became Oman's first World Heritage Site, and after a long restoration it reopened in 2012 for visitors to explore.
